objective: Record that Workbench's MCU CAN Wire V1 and the companion runtime's runtime_can use incompatible classic-CAN payloads on the same arbitration IDs, so no reader assumes the two systems can share one bus.
decision_supported: Whether the two encodings are documented as deliberately incompatible now, and whether adopting one layout or bridging them is a later owner decision.
acceptance: the wire document tabulates both layouts and states they are not interoperable
the TaskEvent integration README states it is not a CAN interoperation claim
a test asserts a foreign runtime_can command frame and a foreign STOP frame are both rejected
no wire constant, schema or codec behaviour changes
evidence: ruff check and ruff format --check pass on the branch
stop_conditions: the change would require modifying a codec, identifier or payload layout
an owner decision is needed about which side owns the bus
the repository schema would need to change
risks_and_fallbacks: The divergence is documented, not fixed; a future reader may still expect interoperation.
Fallback if the two encodings must meet: open a separate decision record and codec change, never relax the version check in place.
The test pins rejection, so an accidental future 'compatibility' fix fails it.
